stemBlocks.value: Two functions are defined by g(x) = 4x + 3 and f(x) = (2x + 7)/(x + 1). (i) State the value of x for which f(x) is undefined. (ii) Calculate the value of gf(5). (iii) Find f⁻¹(x).
Think first: A fraction is undefined only where its denominator is zero — that single idea answers part (i) at once.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p147-q10 from workbook page 147.

solutionSteps.instruction: Set y = f(x) and clear the fraction.
Write the inverse in terms of x.

strategyBlocks.value: Set the denominator of f to zero for part (i), evaluate f(5) and apply g for part (ii), then rearrange y = f(x) to make x the subject for part (iii).

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) f(x) is undefined at x = -1  (ii) gf(5) = 43/3 (≈ 14.3)  (iii) f⁻¹(x) = (7 − x)/(x − 2), x ≠ 2.

whyThisWorks.value: Division by zero has no meaning, so a rational function has a gap in its domain wherever the denominator vanishes. That excluded input reappears as an excluded output of the inverse, and the inverse gains its own exclusion where its denominator is zero. Finding the inverse is always the same routine: clear the fraction, gather the x terms, factor and divide.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting the numerator to zero for part (i) — that gives a root, not an undefined point.
